BSAFs for PCBs and PCDDs and PCBDFs in lake trout in southern Lake Michigan are highly variable and that BSAFs are not necessarily a reliable predictor of the toxicity of a chemical in fish.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a quantitative understanding of the processes that control bioaccumulation of persistent organic pollutants in the aquatic environment.

the development of BSAFs for PCBs, PCDDs, and PCDFs for the southern Lake Michigan food web, and the application of these factors to the development of a bioaccumulation model for PCBs, dioxins, and furans.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the measured BSAFs reflect a balance between chemical-specific metabolism, chemical-specific black carbon affinity, and other unknown chemical-specific processes that affect the measured BSAF.

the measured BSAFs are useful in ranking the relative bioaccumulative potential of individual congeners of PCBs and dioxins/furans, but the BSAFs are not useful as absolute measures of bioaccumulation potential.
BSAFs can be used to predict the relative accumulation potential of PCBs and PCDDs and some PCDFs, but that they should be used with caution for other PCDFs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the BSAFs for PCDDs, PCDFs, and non-ortho and mono-ortho PCBs are not as predictable as previously assumed and that BSAFs are more variable and less consistent than previously assumed.
BSAFs for PCDDs, PCDFs, and non-ortho-PCB congeners can be used to predict bioaccumulation potential for these chemicals in lake trout with a high degree of certainty.
the measured BSAFs are consistent with the hypothesis of slight rates of net net metabolism of some PCBs and PCDDs and/or PCDFs in the southern Lake Michigan fish and food chain.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the first time, we have a set of high-quality BSAFs for PCDDs, PCDFs, and PCBs in a large lake that can be used to evaluate the relative importance of sediment as a source of these chemicals in fish.
, although the BSAF is a powerful tool, it should be applied with caution.
BSAFs can be used as a tool for estimating the relative potential for bioaccumulation of PCDDs, PCDFs, and PCBs.
